questions.question:

• The idiom **White Elephant** means any burdensome, expensive and useless possession that is much more trouble than it is worth.

questions.question:
**Parts of the given sentence have been underlined and given as options. One of them contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.**

It is possible __to prevent oneself__ __with respiratory diseases__ __by maintaining__ __a disciplined lifestyle.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **from respiratory diseases**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace the preposition **'with'** with **'from'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• **'From'** is a preposition, that is used as a function word to indicate physical separation or an act or condition of removal, abstention, exclusion, release, subtraction, or differentiation.
 
 
• **Example -** *He is suffering **from** a headache.*
 
 
 
• The main difference between the part **'with'** and part **'from'** is that the phrase part **'with'** is typically used in reference to objects or possessions, whereas the phrase part **'from'** is typically used in reference to people.
 
• Here in the given sentence, **'from'** is used to explain the theme of the passage, that is **"If an individual person maintains a disciplined lifestyle then it is possible to keep him/her from respiratory diseases"**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 

**Hence, the corrected sentence is:** *It is possible to prevent oneself **from respiratory diseases**__ by maintaining a disciplined lifestyle.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The door was opened by the children for their father.

options.text: The children was opened the door for their father.
The children are opens the door for their father.
The children opened the door for their father.
The children opens the door for their father.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The children opened the door for their father.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive form** and in the **past simple tense**.
 
• The **simple past tense** in the **passive voice** has the following form: **Object + was/were V3 + by + subject.**__
 
• The **simple past tense** in the **active voice** has the following form: __**Subject + V2 + object.**__
 __
 
• **Passive:** *The floor was cleaned by Reema.*
 
• **Active:** *Reema cleaned the floor.*
 
 
 
• In the **active voice of the simple past tense**, we have to change the structure, so the **subject in the passive voice becomes the object in the active voice.**
 
• ​Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3.**

 

**Correct Active Voice:__ ***The children opened the door for their father.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Though he is stout, he runs _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer: **fast.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fast** means moving or capable of moving at high speed.
 
• **“Fast”** is generally used for actions that are more sustained.
 
• Here **"fast"** is an adverb because it modifies the verb **'run'**.
 
• The given sentence is in the simple present form, so **'fast'** (V₁) should be used.
 
 
• **Example -** The athlete runs really **fast**.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3.**

 

**Complete sentence:** *Though he is stout, he runs **fast__**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **"Faster"** is the comparative degree of **"fast"**. It is used when we compare speed between two persons or objects.
 
• **"Fastest"** is the superlative degree of **"fast"**. It is used If we were talking about more than two drives and showing superiority.
 
• The fact is that there is no such word as **“fastly”**. **“Fast”** is already both an adjective and an adverb.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

 

A. Two astronomers – Johannes Kepler from Germany and Galileo from Italy – supported the Copernican theory after nearly a century passed by.

B. Copernicus’ view was that the sun was stationary and the earth and the planets moved in orbits around the sun.

C. Nicholas Copernicus, a Polish priest, proposed a model in 1514.

D. There are many popular theories about the solar system. Ancient People believed that the sun moved around the earth and the earth was static.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"DCBA".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage.
 
• **Statement D** is the opening sentence of the passage which explains **the theories available and what ancient people believed about the movement of the Sun and the Earth.**
 
• **Statement C** is the second sentence of the passage which introduces **Nicholas Copernicus and his proposed model and which year it was proposed.** 
 
• **Statement B** is the third sentence of the passage which explains the **theory of Nicholas Copernicus**.
 
• **Statement A** is the last sentence of the passage which shows that **other astronomers like,** **Johannes Kepler and Galileo supported the Copernican theory after nearly a century passed.​**
 
• Hence, the correct sequence is **D, C, B, A.**

 

**The correct passage is:** ***D.** There are many popular theories about the solar system. Ancient People believed that the sun moved around the earth and the earth was static. **C.** Nicholas Copernicus, a Polish priest, proposed a model in 1514. **B.** Copernicus’ view was that the sun was stationary and the earth and the planets moved in orbits around the sun. **A.** Two astronomers – Johannes Kepler from Germany and Galileo from Italy – supported the Copernican theory after nearly a century passed by.*

__
 
• **'Them'** (pronoun) is used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to two or more people or things previously mentioned or easily identified.

 
 
• ***For example -** I bathed the kids and read **them** stories.*
 
 
 
• Here, in the given paragraph the word **'them'** refers to **"the papers."**
 
• So, it is clear that the most appropriate word is **'them'**.

What she had managed to collect was mostly press cuttings and articles (4) __**downloaded**__ from the Internet. She took the papers and dropped** (5) __them__** in a desk drawer.
